The W-4 is completed by the worker and instructs the employer’s withholding going forward. The W-2 reports afterwards what was paid and withheld, the 1099 reports non-employee payments, and the 1040 is the return that reconciles everything at the end of the year.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The response says the work is wrong but not where or why.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response locates the first wrong step and states the misconception behind it.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response locates the error, names the misconception, and gives a check that would have caught it.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The method from the earlier case is restated without being applied.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The method is applied but a difference in the new case is ignored.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The method is applied and adjusted for what is different in the new case.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The method is applied, adjusted, and the limit of the transfer is stated.

judgment.prompt: The filer did nothing wrong and still owes $2,044.00 at filing. Explain how that happens, and describe two different things the filer could have done during the year to avoid being surprised by it.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that withholding is set per employer against that employer’s payments, so income reported on a 1099 has nothing withheld and the shortfall only appears when the 1040 combines both.
Gives two distinct actions — adjusting the W-4 so the employer withholds more, or setting money aside from each 1099 payment as it arrives — and connects each to the $2,044.00 figure.
Notes that this is a timing and cash-planning problem rather than an extra tax: the same $4,144.00 was owed either way.
evidenceRequirements: Uses the $4,144.00 total tax, the $2,100 withheld, and the $2,044.00 owed.
lookFors: The response distinguishes owing tax from owing a penalty; nothing here says the filer was penalised.
The response recognises that the employer had no way to know about the 1099 income.
judgment.commonMisconception: Assuming that because tax is withheld from a paycheck, all tax for the year has been paid.

nonDiagnosticGuard: Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
